sessions.assessment: The R1 synthesizer fully receives the four private reports, their shared-block-decoded evidence and six same-wave paired comparisons. It materially corrects G1's shifted interval indexing and uses the right group-mean pool minimum 0.794504 A for the 0.02 A band. It chooses [3,3,5,5], [7,7,5,5], [7,3,5,5], [5,3,5,7], building a 3/5/7 early-control scan on one background plus a matched control-1 bracket. This is constructive experiment design. However, it publishes new unsupported restrictions: joint changes allegedly require range expansion even though two controls are already allowed; different signs on different controls are treated as lack of a monotone response; and small responses inside the ranking band are called physically unresolved. Its claim that control 1 has only tick 5 sampled contradicts the executed [5,3,5,5].
sessions.decision_update: R2 executes all four selected arrays. The matched control-1 bracket at early tick 7 gives condition 0.794708585/0.795293748/0.795612933 A and gaps 3.626230488/3.626228056/3.626030293 for ticks 3/5/7 respectively. These are continuous trade-offs, not proof of a dead control axis. The chosen [7,7,5,5] has the best functional gap within the final condition band, but this does not support the synthesizer's claims about which mechanism fixed residual error. A capability improvement should make public memory an evidence-scoped response model, retaining the correct boundary correction while preventing global axis-exhaustion and action-contract claims from a few local observations.
sessions.counterexample_or_limitation: The synthesizer explicitly rejects the private no-op explanation and does not modify the submitted arrays, showing valuable oversight. It also explicitly recognizes the untested control-2 down-direction. Its quoted single-candidate gain 0.0259 is not the contribution to the mean (about 0.0010365), and a requirement for coherent movement across many candidates would improperly discount concentrated gains. The comparison between sub-milliangstrom error and a dimensionless matching-switch fraction is not a noise calibration. The late up-probe and the previous late down-probe have different control-1 backgrounds, so they do not form a clean same-background bracket.
